Subject: Re: Encryption custody and key control for private deployment

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are progressing with an internal approvals package for HelioBank's private deployment (VPC + customer-managed KMS). Before we sign off on the design, our legal and infosec teams have asked for a short annex for the DPA that clarifies:

- Who holds operational custody of customer keys (Redwood operator vs. customer KMS).
- Break-glass operator access: conditions, approvals, and least-privilege scope.
- Telemetry and traces that Redwood might collect (are model inputs redactable?).
- Subprocessor list for Private deployments and any planned cross-border transfers (EU -> US).

Could you provide a playbook or annex draft we can review? Also curious whether you support an escrow or sealed-encryption option for long-term legal hold.

If you can send a short proposal by EOD Wednesday (11/4) that would help our procurement timeline.

Best,
Allison

Senior Counsel, HelioBank

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Encryption custody and key control for private deployment

Allison —

Thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on the ask. I	m putting together a lightweight "Encryption custody playbook" and a short DPA annex that explicitly covers: custody model options, operator break-glass runbook, telemetry minimization, and a subprocessor registry with geo-transfer commitments.

High-level options we	plan to propose:
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended): keys never leave customer's KMS; Redwood gets only ephemeral wrapping keys for specific ops; full audit trail.
- Customer-held keys with escrow: customer retains exclusive cryptographic control, Redwood can request sealed-escrow under court order (process in annex).
- Customer-controlled key with emergency operator unwrap: explicit two-person approval, justification log, and automatic revocation timeline (48 hrs max unless extended by legal).

I'll attach draft artifacts: custody-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook), subprocessor-list-20261102.csv, and dpa-crossborder-annex-draft.docx.

One internal ask: can I loop in Kim (security) and Marissa (legal ops) to confirm telemetry redaction text and operator entitlements? Karthik, can you validate the operator runbook language around break-glass and audit retention?

I'll follow up with a consolidated email and an annotated annex by EOD Wednesday.

Cheers,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Team —

Looping you in per Allison's request (HelioBank). They need an annex for the DPA by EOD Wed (11/4). Key asks below and a 24–48h turnaround would be ideal:

1) Operator break-glass runbook (Karthik): need exact approval flow, who is allowed to call break-glass, what evidence is logged, and how we limit scope to a single customer environment. Include retention windows for unwrapped blobs and the rollback path.

2) Telemetry and redaction (Kimberly): they want assurance inputs that feed models can be redacted at the prefix/token level; need sample wording for the DPA about "no retention of PII in traces" and what telemetry fields we store for performance troubleshooting.

3) Legal/Procure wording (Marissa): short clause for the annex covering cross-border transfers (EU -> US), standard SCCs vs. EEA customer choice, and a sealed-escrow option paragraph for legal hold scenarios. Also confirm that our subprocessor list is accurate for private deployments.

I attached the custody playbook v1 and a current subprocessor list. Karthik, note we plan to include operator MFA + hardware token requirement and an audit-only privileged access channel (no shell; API-only with JIT).

Please reply inline with redlines or short bullet answers. I'll synthesize and send to Allison.

Thanks — Mateo

Attachment references: custody-playbook-v1.pdf, subprocessor-list-20261102.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Encryption custody and key control for private deployment

Mateo —

Draft language (high level): we will only collect operational telemetry necessary to meet SLAs and to diagnose infra issues. PII fields will be redacted at ingestion; we will persist request metadata (timestamp, model id, request size, latency) and limited trace IDs. Retention: 30 days for detailed traces, 12 months for aggregated metrics.

We should add a short sentence: "Customer has the ability to opt-in to extend trace retention for incident investigation provided mutually agreed controls are in place."

Marissa: flagging SCCs question — if Helio is EEA-based they can require SCCs and we should offer the EU data routing and an EU-hosted private control plane option.

— Kim

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Encryption custody and key control for private deployment

Mateo/Kim/Karthik —

I reviewed the annex draft. Proposed inserts:
- Cross-border: we offer SCCs + EU-hosted control plane; include explicit commitment that customer data for HelioBank will not be transferred outside the EEA except under SCCs or customer instruction.
- Escrow: limited clause for sealed-escrow with court-order release; add requirement for customer notif within 7 days of any legal access to keys.
- Subprocessors: attach the CSV and add a clause to notify customers 30 days before adding any subprocessor that will process customer ML inputs.

Send me the redline and I'll inline. If they need legal certified language we can route to contracts but this should be sufficient for procurement to move forward.

— Marissa
